cards.explanation: The answer is a thief and a robber. Jesus says whoever "…climbs in some other way, is a thief and a robber." (John 10:1). Think about that, friends. There's a gate right there, and this guy picks the climbing. That's like sneaking in my bakery window when the front door is sitting there.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "…the one who enters by the gate is the shepherd of the sheep." (John 10:2). The shepherd walks right in the front. No ladder, no sneaking, no hiding behind a flour sack. Simple as that.

The word is "own." Jesus says the shepherd "…calls his own sheep by name and leads them out." (John 10:3). These aren't just any sheep. They're his, and he knows each one well enough to use their name, which is more than I can say for me and the names of my cookie batches.

The answer is that he goes on ahead of them. Jesus says the shepherd "…goes on ahead of them, and his sheep follow him…" (John 10:4). He leads, and they trail after. No pushing and no herding from the back. He's up front, and they know it.

The answer is that they run away from him. Jesus says the sheep "…will never follow a stranger; in fact, they will flee from him because they do not recognize his voice." (John 10:5). They don't stop to chat, friends. They're GONE. A voice they don't know is a voice they don't follow.

The answer is False. The people listening did not understand. John says, "…they did not understand what He was telling them." (John 10:6). Jesus doesn't walk away from them, though. He says it again, in a new way, in John 10:7.

The answer is the gate for the sheep. Jesus says, "…I am the gate for the sheep." (John 10:7). Remember how the shepherd comes in by the gate? Now Jesus says He is the gate itself. Plain words this time, and nothing left to guess.

The answer is False. The sheep did not listen to them. Jesus says all who came before Him were thieves and robbers, "…but the sheep did not listen to them." (John 10:8). That ties right back to the stranger's voice in John 10:5. The sheep know who they're listening for.

The answer is that he will be saved. Jesus says, "If anyone enters through Me, he will be saved." (John 10:9). Notice the word "anyone," friends. He goes on to say that person "…will come in and go out and find pasture."

The word is "life." Jesus says, "I have come that they may have life, and have it in all its fullness." (John 10:10). Compare that with the thief, who "…comes only to steal and kill and destroy." One takes, and One gives. Fullness means the whole batch, not a crumb.

The answer is that He lays down His life for them. Jesus says, "The good shepherd lays down His life for the sheep." (John 10:11). I think this one is heavy, friends, so I'll say it plain. He doesn't only guide the sheep. He gives His own life for them.

The word is "abandons." Jesus says, "When he sees the wolf coming, he abandons the sheep and runs away." (John 10:12). That's the hired hand, and the sheep aren't his own. When trouble shows up, he's already looking for the exit.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "The man runs away because he is a hired servant and is unconcerned for the sheep." (John 10:13). The sheep aren't his own, and he doesn't care about them. When the wolf shows up, he's gone, and he doesn't look back (John 10:12). That's the big difference between him and the good shepherd.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "I know My sheep and My sheep know Me, just as the Father knows Me and I know the Father" (John 10:14-15). Let that sink in, friends. He's comparing it to how He and the Father know each other. That's no casual hello at the gate.

The word is "voice." Jesus says of His other sheep, "…they will listen to My voice." (John 10:16). Voice has been the word all the way through this picture. Back in John 10:4 the sheep follow the shepherd because they know his voice. Same idea, and it covers sheep who aren't in this fold yet.

The answer is one flock with one shepherd. Jesus says, "Then there will be one flock and one shepherd." (John 10:16). He has sheep that are not of this fold, and He must bring them in as well. When He does, it all becomes one flock. One flock and one shepherd, friends.

The answer is to take it up again. Jesus says, "…I lay down My life in order to take it up again." (John 10:17). Laying it down isn't the end of the sentence. He says it's so He can take it up again. I'll let His words stand just as He said them.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "No one takes it from Me, but I lay it down of My own accord." (John 10:18). He also says He has authority to lay it down and to take it up again. It's a charge He received from His Father.

The answer is that a demon can't open blind eyes. Some say Jesus is demon-possessed, but others say, "These are not the words of a man possessed by a demon. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?" (John 10:21). They point to the opening of blind eyes as their reason. A question like that is hard to argue with.
